lessons.title: Past of to be: was and were
lessons.summary: Talk about where people were and how things were.

sections.title: was / were
sections.body_md:
| | past of *to be* |
|---|---|
| I / he / she / it | **was** |
| you / we / they | **were** |

**Negative:** *wasn't* (was not), *weren't* (were not).

**Question:** ***Was** it cold? **Were** they at home?*

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *I **was** at the doctor's yesterday.*
- *The film **was** really funny.*
- *We **weren't** at school last Friday.*
- ***Were** you tired after the trip?* — *Yes, I **was**.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.explanation: *The shop* = *it*, so the question starts with *Was*.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

lessons.title: Past simple: regular verbs
lessons.summary: Add -ed to talk about finished actions.

sections.title: Finished actions
sections.body_md:
We use the **past simple** for actions that finished in the past.

Regular verbs add **-ed**, the same for everyone: *I work**ed**, she work**ed**, they work**ed**.*

Spelling:
- *live → live**d*** (ends in *e*: add *d*)
- *study → stud**ied*** (consonant + *y*: *y → ied*)
- *stop → stop**ped*** (short verb, one vowel + one consonant: double it)
- *play → play**ed*** (vowel + *y*: just add *ed*)

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md: *Last weekend I **visited** my aunt. We **cooked** lunch and **watched** a film. On Sunday it **rained**, so I **stayed** at home and **studied**.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: She ___ in Rome for two years.
Which sentence is in the past?
He ___ for the exam all night.

lessons.title: Past simple: irregular verbs
lessons.summary: Learn common verbs that do not use -ed.

sections.title: Irregular verbs
sections.body_md:
Many common verbs have a special past form. Learn them by heart.

| verb | past | verb | past |
|---|---|---|---|
| go | **went** | have | **had** |
| see | **saw** | eat | **ate** |
| come | **came** | make | **made** |
| take | **took** | buy | **bought** |
| get | **got** | write | **wrote** |
| say | **said** | think | **thought** |

sections.title: A story
sections.body_md: *On Saturday I **went** to the market. I **saw** my friend Leo there. We **bought** some fruit and **had** coffee. Then we **took** the bus home. Leo **said** it **was** a great day.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.prompt: I ___ a letter to my grandmother.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: She ___ a new phone last week.
I ___ a strange noise in the night.

lessons.title: Past simple: questions and negatives
lessons.summary: Use did and didn't to ask and say no about the past.

sections.title: did / didn't
sections.body_md:
- **Negative:** *didn't* + base verb: *I **didn't go** to work.* (not *didn't went*)
- **Question:** *Did* + subject + base verb: ***Did** you **see** the match?*
- **Short answers:** *Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.*
- **Wh- questions:** *Where **did** you **go**? What **did** she **buy**?*

With *was/were* we do **not** use *did*: *Were you tired?* (not *Did you be tired?*)

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- ***Did** you **enjoy** the concert?* — *Yes, I **did**.*
- *She **didn't like** the food.*
- *What time **did** the train **leave**?*
- *We **didn't have** time for lunch.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.explanation: After *didn't*, use the base verb: *didn't finish*.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

lessons.title: Yesterday, last week, two days ago
lessons.summary: Say when something happened.

sections.title: When did it happen?
sections.body_md:
- **yesterday** / **yesterday morning**
- **last** + time: *last night, last week, last year* (no *the*)
- time + **ago**: *two days ago, ten minutes ago*
- **in** + year or month: *in 2019, in May*
- **on** + day or date: *on Monday, on 3 March*

These words usually go at the end or the start of the sentence.

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *I started this job **three months ago**.*
- ***Last summer** we went camping.*
- *She was born **in** 2001.*
- *I saw him **on** Tuesday.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.hint: Which word comes after the time?

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

options: I saw him the last week.

lessons.title: Present continuous: happening now
lessons.summary: Say what people are doing at the moment.

sections.title: am / is / are + -ing
sections.body_md:
We use the **present continuous** for actions happening **now** or around now.

*I **am** read**ing**. She **is** cook**ing**. They **are** play**ing**.*

Spelling: *make → mak**ing*** (drop *e*), *run → run**ning*** (double the consonant), *lie → l**ying***.

**Negative:** *I'm not working. He isn't sleeping.*  **Question:** ***Are** you listen**ing**?*

sections.title: Look out of the window
sections.body_md:
*It **is raining**. A man **is running** for the bus. Two children **are playing** in the park. My neighbour **isn't working** today: she **is sitting** in her garden.*

Words like *now, right now, at the moment, look!, listen!* often go with it.

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.explanation: Short verb, one vowel + one consonant: double it: *swimming*.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: He ___ today. He is at home.

lessons.title: Present simple or present continuous?
lessons.summary: Choose between habits and things happening now.

sections.title: Habit or now?
sections.body_md:
- **Present simple**: habits, routines and facts: *I **drink** coffee every morning.*
- **Present continuous**: now or around now: *I**'m drinking** tea now.*

Clue words:
- simple: *every day, usually, often, never, on Mondays*
- continuous: *now, at the moment, today, this week*

Some verbs are rarely used with -ing: *like, love, want, know, understand, need*: *I **want** a coffee* (not *I'm wanting*).

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *Ali usually **walks** to work, but today he**'s taking** the bus.*
- *Water **boils** at 100 °C.*
- *I **know** the answer.*
- *We**'re staying** with friends this week.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.prompt: She ___ to the gym every Tuesday.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: My brother ___ for an exam this week.

exercises.explanation: *never* = a habit: present simple. *We* has no *-s*.

lessons.title: Going to: plans and intentions
lessons.summary: Talk about things you have decided to do.

sections.title: be going to + verb
sections.body_md:
Use **be going to** for plans you have already made, and for things we can see are going to happen.

*I**'m going to** visit my cousin. She**'s going to** study law. They**'re going to** move house.*

**Negative:** *I'm not going to ...*  **Question:** ***Are** you **going to** ...?*

Look at those clouds! It**'s going to** rain. (we can see it)

sections.title: Plans for the summer
sections.body_md: *This summer **I'm going to** learn to drive. My sister **is going to** work in a hotel. We **aren't going to** travel abroad, but we **are going to** visit the coast for a weekend.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.prompt: We ___ paint the kitchen next weekend.

exercises.explanation: We can see it is about to happen: *are going to*.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: I ___ to the party. I'm too tired.

exercises.explanation: Question: *What are you going to do?*

lessons.title: Will: predictions, offers and quick decisions
lessons.summary: Use will for the future when you decide now or guess.

sections.title: will + verb
sections.body_md:
**will** (*'ll*) + base verb is the same for everyone: *I'll help, she'll help.*

Use it for:
- **quick decisions** made now: *The phone's ringing. I**'ll** answer it.*
- **offers and promises**: *I**'ll** carry that bag for you. I **won't** tell anyone.*
- **predictions** (what you think): *I think it **will** be sunny tomorrow.*

**Negative:** *won't* (= will not).

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *"I'm cold." "I**'ll** close the window."*
- *Don't worry, I **won't** be late.*
- *I think you**'ll** love this book.*
- ***Will** you help me with this?*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.prompt: "I haven't got any money." "Don't worry, I ___ pay."
exercises.explanation: A quick decision or offer made now: *I'll pay*.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: I think people ___ live on Mars one day.

exercises.explanation: An offer made now: *I'll help you*.

lessons.title: Tomorrow, next week, in two days
lessons.summary: Say when something will happen.

sections.title: When will it happen?
sections.body_md:
- **tomorrow** / **tomorrow morning** / **the day after tomorrow**
- **next** + time: *next week, next month, next year* (no *the*)
- **in** + period: *in two days, in an hour* (= two days from now)
- **soon**, **later**, **tonight**, **this evening**

Compare: *two days **ago*** (past) and ***in** two days* (future).

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *The shop opens **in** ten minutes.*
- *I'll call you **tomorrow**.*
- *We're going to Italy **next** month.*
- *See you **later**!*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: She's starting a new job ___ month.

exercises.explanation: *in three days* = three days from now.

exercises.prompt: "When is the party?" "___ Saturday, the day after tomorrow."
I'm busy now. I'll do it ___.

lessons.title: Comparatives: bigger, more expensive
lessons.summary: Compare two people or things.

sections.title: Comparing two things
sections.body_md:
- Short adjectives: add **-er** + **than**: *tall → tall**er** than*
- Ending in *e*: *nice → nic**er***
- One vowel + one consonant: double it: *big → big**ger***, *hot → hot**ter***
- Ending in consonant + *y*: *happy → happ**ier***, *easy → eas**ier***
- Long adjectives: **more** + adjective: *more expensive, more interesting*
- Irregular: *good → **better***, *bad → **worse***, *far → **further / farther***

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *My brother is **taller than** me.*
- *Trains are **faster than** buses.*
- *This book is **more interesting than** the film.*
- *Today's weather is **worse than** yesterday's.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.prompt: An elephant is ___ than a horse.

sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

lessons.title: Superlatives: the biggest, the most beautiful
lessons.summary: Say which is number one in a group.

sections.title: The top of a group
sections.body_md:
Use a **superlative** to compare one thing with all the others in a group. Use **the**.

- Short: **the** + adjective + **-est**: *the tall**est***, *the big**gest***, *the happ**iest***
- Long: **the most** + adjective: *the most beautiful*
- Irregular: *good → **the best***, *bad → **the worst***

We often use **in** with places and groups: *the tallest building **in** the city*.

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *Mount Everest is **the highest** mountain in the world.*
- *This is **the most delicious** cake I know.*
- *Who is **the best** player in your team?*
- *January is **the coldest** month here.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.explanation: Number one in the group: *the fastest*.

exercises.prompt: That was ___ day of my life!

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: She is ___ student in the class.
Last winter was ___ winter for fifty years.

lessons.title: Adverbs: quickly, carefully, well
lessons.summary: Say how someone does something.

sections.title: How?
sections.body_md:
An **adverb of manner** says **how** we do something. Many are adjective + **-ly**: *quick → quick**ly***, *careful → careful**ly***.

- *-y → -ily*: *easy → eas**ily***, *happy → happ**ily***
- Irregular: *good → **well***, *fast → **fast***, *hard → **hard***

Adjectives describe **nouns**; adverbs describe **verbs**: *She is a **careful** driver. She drives **carefully**.*

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *Please speak **slowly**.*
- *He plays the piano very **well**.*
- *The children waited **quietly**.*
- *She works **hard**.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.prompt: He ran ___ to catch the bus.
exercises.hint: Does the word describe the verb?
exercises.explanation: *ran* is a verb, so we need an adverb: *quickly*.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.explanation: Before a noun we need an adjective: *a hard worker*.
*fast* is the same as an adjective and an adverb.

lessons.title: Countable and uncountable nouns
lessons.summary: Use a, some and any with nouns you can and can't count.

sections.title: Can you count it?
sections.body_md:
- **Countable** nouns have a plural: *an apple → apples, a chair → chairs*.
- **Uncountable** nouns have no plural and no *a/an*: *water, rice, money, information, advice, bread, music*.

- **some** in positive sentences: *some apples, some water*
- **any** in negatives and questions: *I don't have **any** money. Is there **any** milk?*

We can count uncountable things with containers: *a bottle of water, a piece of advice, a slice of bread*.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body_md: *We have **some** eggs and **some** cheese, but we don't have **any** bread. Is there **any** milk? Can you buy **a loaf of** bread and **a carton of** milk?*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

I bought ___ oranges at the market.

exercises.explanation: Count bread with *a slice of* or *a loaf of*.

lessons.title: How much, how many, a lot of
lessons.summary: Talk about quantity.

sections.title: much / many / a lot of
sections.body_md:
- **many** + plural countable: *many books*
- **much** + uncountable: *much time*
- **a lot of** + both: *a lot of books, a lot of time*

*much* and *many* are most common in **questions and negatives**: *I don't have **much** time. Were there **many** people?*

Questions: ***How many** brothers have you got? **How much** money do you need?*

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- ***How many** students are in your class?* — *About twenty.*
- ***How much** does this cost?*
- *There was **a lot of** traffic this morning.*
- *We didn't take **many** photos.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: There are ___ trees in this park.

options: She has a lot of friends.

exercises.explanation: *a lot of* + plural: *a lot of friends*.

lessons.title: Object pronouns: me, him, them
lessons.summary: Use the right pronoun after a verb or a preposition.

sections.title: Subject and object
sections.body_md:
A **subject** pronoun does the action. An **object** pronoun comes **after** a verb or a preposition.

| Subject | Object |
|---|---|
| I | me |
| you | you |
| he | him |
| she | her |
| it | it |
| we | us |
| they | them |

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *I like **her**.* (not *I like she*)
- *Can you help **me**?*
- *This present is for **them**.*
- *We called **him** yesterday.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.prompt: Tom is my friend. I see ___ every day.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

This is my new phone. Do you like ___?

lessons.title: Must and have to
lessons.summary: Talk about rules and things that are necessary.

sections.title: Rules and needs
sections.body_md:
- **must** + verb: a strong rule, or the speaker feels it is necessary: *I **must** call my mum.*
- **have to / has to** + verb: necessary because of a rule or situation: *She **has to** wear a uniform.*
- **mustn't**: it is not allowed: *You **mustn't** smoke here.*
- **don't have to**: it is not necessary (you can choose): *You **don't have to** come.*

Past: use **had to**: *We **had to** wait an hour.*

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *Students **must** switch off their phones in the exam room.*
- *He **has to** get up at six for work.*
- *You **mustn't** touch the paintings.*
- *It's Sunday, so I **don't have to** work.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: You ___ cross the road when the light is red. It's dangerous.

lessons.title: Should for advice
lessons.summary: Give and ask for advice.

sections.title: Giving advice
sections.body_md:
Use **should** + verb to say something is a good idea. Use **shouldn't** for a bad idea.

*should* is the same for every person: *I / you / she / they **should** rest.*

Ask for advice: ***Should** I take a taxi?* · *What **should** I do?*

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *You look tired. You **should** go to bed early.*
- *You **shouldn't** eat so much sugar.*
- *What **should** I wear to the interview?*
- *She **should** see a doctor.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.prompt: You have a cold. You ___ drink hot tea.
He ___ drive so fast. It's dangerous.

sections.title: Check
sections.body_md: Answer the questions.

exercises.prompt: ___ I call her now or later?
You ___ stay up late before an exam.

lessons.title: Linking words: and, but, because, so
lessons.summary: Join two ideas in one sentence.

sections.title: Joining ideas
sections.body_md:
- **and** adds an idea: *I like tea **and** coffee.*
- **but** shows a contrast: *It's small **but** comfortable.*
- **because** gives a reason: *I stayed home **because** I was ill.*
- **so** gives a result: *I was ill, **so** I stayed home.*

Tip: *because* answers *Why?* · *so* tells you *what happened next*.

sections.title: Examples
sections.body_md:
- *She plays the piano **and** sings.*
- *I wanted to go, **but** I was busy.*
- *We took a taxi **because** it was raining.*
- *It was raining, **so** we took a taxi.*

sections.title: Try it
sections.body_md: Try it.

exercises.explanation: Cheap vs. good is a surprise: *but*.

lessons.title: Writing a short story: first, then, after that
lessons.summary: Put events in order in a short paragraph.

sections.title: Telling events in order
sections.body_md:
Use **sequence words** to show the order of events:

- **First,** ...
- **Then** / **Next,** ...
- **After that,** ...
- **Finally,** ... (the last thing)

Use the **past simple** for a story about yesterday or last week. Put a comma after *First*, *After that* and *Finally*.

sections.title: Example paragraph
sections.body_md: *Last Saturday was a busy day. **First,** I cleaned my flat. **Then** I went to the market and bought some fruit. **After that,** I met my friend for lunch. **Finally,** we watched a film in the evening.*

*Next* and *Then* both mean the following step.
